## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Only optional test corrections were found in the reviewed scope. The tests leave nested basename matching unverified and assert internal parser values for the default and repeated flag cases.

## Changes

The CLI adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that filters files by basename and logs skips in verbose mode. The pull request documents the flag and adds tests for parsing, filtering, and archive contents.

## Suggestions

- cli/main.py:33 — tests — Cover exact-name exclusions in nested directories — For `--exclude skip.log`, a regression that matches relative paths would archive `nested/skip.log` because `nested/skip.log` does not match `skip.log`. Every exclusion test places matching files at the source root. — Users who exclude files by basename have no regression coverage for matches below the source root.
- tests/test_main.py:20 — tests — Verify repeated exclusions in the archive — With `--exclude '*.log' --exclude '*.tmp'`, this assertion rejects a tuple containing both patterns. The archive test passes only one flag. — The suite can reject a compatible parser refactor and miss a CLI wiring regression that applies only one of two flags. — Fix: Extend `test_main_leaves_excluded_files_out_of_the_archive` to exercise both flags in one invocation.
- tests/test_main.py:24 — tests — Verify archive contents with no exclusion flag — An invocation without `--exclude` would fail this assertion if the parser returned `()` as the empty pattern set. `collect` already accepts that value. — The assertion constrains the parser’s internal default and leaves archive membership unverified when users omit the flag.
